title: Robot Collisions
statement:
There are `n` robots on a straight line, numbered in the order they are given. Robot `i` starts at `positions[i]` with health `healths[i]` and heads in direction `directions[i]`, either `'L'` (left) or `'R'` (right). The starting positions are all different but are not necessarily sorted.

All robots start moving at the same moment and at the same speed, and never turn around. When two robots reach the same point at the same time, they collide:

- if their healths differ, the one with less health is removed, and the other loses exactly 1 health and carries on in its own direction;
- if their healths are equal, both are removed.

When no further collision can happen, return the healths of the robots still on the line, listed in input order (robot `0` first, then robot `1`, and so on). If no robot is left, return an empty list.
constraints: All values in positions are distinct
signature: List<Integer> survivedRobotsHealths(int[] positions, int[] healths, String directions)
notes:
## Intuition

Only a right-mover that is to the left of a left-mover can ever meet it, so first sort the robots by position. Sweeping from left to right, keep the right-movers that are still alive on a stack. A left-mover first meets the nearest right-mover behind it, which is the top of the stack. If it wins, it carries on and meets the next one down; if it loses or ties, it is gone. A left-mover that empties the stack runs off to the left and never meets anyone again. This is the same pattern as "Asteroid Collision", with health instead of size. A slower alternative resolves collisions one at a time, always taking the facing pair with the smallest gap, which costs O(n²).

## Approach

1. Copy `healths` into `health` and sort the robot indices by position into `order`.
2. For each robot `i` in `order`: a right-mover is pushed onto `stack`.
3. A left-mover fights the robot at the top of `stack` while both exist:
   - weaker top: it is removed (health `0`, popped) and `i` loses 1;
   - stronger top: it loses 1 and `i` is removed;
   - equal: both are removed.
4. Robots with health `0` are gone; return the other healths in index order.

## Example 1, step by step

All five robots move right, so every one is pushed onto the stack and no left-mover ever arrives. Nothing collides, and `health` is still `[2, 17, 9, 15, 10]`, which is returned in input order.

Example 2 shows a fight: in position order the robots are `2` (R, 15), `0` (R, 10), `1` (L, 10), `3` (L, 12). Robot `1` ties with robot `0` and both vanish; robot `3` then meets robot `2`, which wins and drops to `14`. The answer is `[14]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; each robot is pushed and popped at most once, so the sweep is O(n).
- Space: O(n) for `order`, `health` and `stack`.

## Pitfalls

- The input positions are not sorted, yet the answer must follow the input order: sort indices, not values.
- A strong left-mover can destroy several right-movers in a row; use a loop, not a single check.
- Equal healths remove both robots, and then the left-mover must stop.
- Two robots moving the same way never collide, and a left-mover that survives is not pushed: nothing to its left can reach it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of robots |
| `health` | current health of each robot; `0` means removed |
| `order` | robot indices sorted by position |
| `stack` | right-movers seen so far that are still alive, nearest on top |
| `i` | the robot being processed |
| `top` | the right-mover the left-mover `i` is fighting |
